cases.counterfactual_program:
(rule! (lambda (g)
         (let* ((h (rows g))
                (w (cols g)))
           (let* ((reds (for*/list ((r (range 0 h)) (c (range 0 w)) #:when (= (at g r c) 2))
                          (list r c)))
                  (pairs (for*/list ((i (range 0 (length reds))) (j (range (+ i 1) (length reds)))
                             #:when
                             (let ((a (list-ref reds i))
                                   (bb (list-ref reds j)))
                               (or (= (first a) (first bb)) (= (second a) (second bb)))))
                           (list (list-ref reds i) (list-ref reds j))))
                  (trunk-pair (first pairs))
                  (t1 (first trunk-pair))
                  (t2 (second trunk-pair))
                  (result (make-hash)))
             (for* ((r (range 0 h)) (c (range 0 w)))
                   (hash-set! result (list r c) (at g r c)))
             (if (= (second t1) (second t2))
                 (let ((tc (/ w 2))
                       (r1 (min (first t1) (first t2)))
                       (r2 (max (first t1) (first t2))))
                   (for ((r (range (+ r1 1) r2))) (hash-set! result (list r tc) 3))
                   (for ((red reds))
                     (when
                       (and (not (equal? red t1)) (not (equal? red t2)))
                       (let ((rr (first red))
                             (rc (second red)))
                         (if (< rc tc)
                             (for ((cc (range (+ rc 1) tc)))
                               (hash-set! result (list rr cc) 3))
                             (for ((cc (range (+ tc 1) rc)))
                               (hash-set! result (list rr cc) 3)))))))
                 (let ((tr (/ h 2))
                       (c1 (min (second t1) (second t2)))
                       (c2 (max (second t1) (second t2))))
                   (for ((cc (range (+ c1 1) c2))) (hash-set! result (list tr cc) 3))
                   (for ((red reds))
                     (when
                       (and (not (equal? red t1)) (not (equal? red t2)))
                       (let ((rr (first red))
                             (rc (second red)))
                         (if (< rr tr)
                             (for ((r (range (+ rr 1) tr)))
                               (hash-set! result (list r rc) 3))
                             (for ((r (range (+ tr 1) rr)))
                               (hash-set! result (list r rc) 3))))))))
             (cellmap g (r c v) (hash-ref result (list r c) 0))))))

intermediate_value.interpretation: Author-derived geometry. Native witness construction and replay verify both final labels; they do not independently certify this causal interpretation.

intermediate: The input-derived trunk endpoints, orientation, perpendicular line coordinate and endpoint span; these give each remaining red cell its branch role and side of the trunk.
step_a: Find the unique row- or column-aligned pair of red cells, then derive its trunk orientation, line and span from the current input.
step_b: Fill the inferred trunk span and connect each branch along the perpendicular axis, toward the inferred trunk line or away from that line to the canvas edge according to the episode setting.
why_b_depends_on_a: The same branch position can lie on either side of a trunk found elsewhere in the input. Replacing the inferred line by the canvas midpoint changes both trunk pixels and the later branch routing. The exact intervention retains red scanning, pair selection, orientation and painting code; it changes only the consumed line coordinate. This is a geometry-derived dependency, not iterative state simulation.
